newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up on buying of second-tier stocks.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up on buying of second-tier stocks.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed higher Friday, as local investors bought second- and third-tier stocks, brokers said.
They added prices would probably be broadly stable Monday.
Friday, the General Index .IGRA rose 0.76 percent to 1,651.68 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL climbed 1.04 percent to 2,380.36 points.
"Investors are buying selectively depending how they judge specific companies," Jaime Jarra of local brokerage said, adding the most attractive sectors was contruction.

Brokers also said Friday's rise signaled an end to recent falls caused by fears that interest rates would rise in the United States and make bonds more attractive to foreign investors than emerging market stocks.
Investors assumed the Federal Reserve would hike rates and the market has now adjusted to this as if the rise had already been announced, they said.
In a total of 1,646 trades, volume was 32.0 million soles ($12.1 million), where 37 stocks rose, 28 remained stable and 24 fell, according to preliminary figures.
Among blue chip stocks, benchmark Telefnica del Per "B" rose 0.68 percent to 5.88 soles in a modest 22 percent of the the session's volume.
Cementos Lima closed up 0.89 percent at 4.55 soles on low volume of 13,00 shares.
Peru's largest cement company announced during the session it would issue up to $60 million of bonds to finance its production plant's expansion.

Backus y Johnston, the country's largest brewery, climbed 2.04 percent to 2.50 soles in volume of 431,000 shares. The country's largest brewer announced earlier Friday JP Morgan would lend it $100 million to refinance its debts.
